candidate.answerReason: The two occupied playing places provide 180 minutes of combined individual playing time. Dividing equally among five children gives 36 minutes each.

methods.label: Share the combined playing time
methods.explanation:
Think of the game as having two playing places, each occupied for \(90\) minutes. Together, these provide
\[
90+90=180
\]
minutes of individual playing time. Every minute a child plays contributes to this combined total.

Since the five children receive equal playing time, each plays
\[
180\div5=\boxed{36\text{ minutes}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses addition to total two simultaneous playing places, followed by equal-sharing division.

candidate.annotationRationale: The requested quantity is an equal share of combined playing time, matching cnm_p084. The total-as-sum relationship in cnm_p111 supports accounting for both occupied places. The local prerequisites are the equal-sharing meaning of division and calculating a three-digit number divided by a one-digit number.

review.mathematicalCheck: Two occupied playing places over 90 minutes supply 180 minutes of individual playing time. Equal sharing among five children therefore gives 180 ÷ 5 = 36 minutes each. The explanation correctly accounts for simultaneous play.
review.levelCheck: Adding the two time totals and dividing equally fits AMC 8.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_p084 matches equal-sharing division. cnm_p111 explicitly includes total-as-sum relationships, and the division prerequisites fit the calculation.
